title: 1.3. The First Program & The print() Function
summary: Learn how the print() built-in function works, pass arguments, handle whitespace, and explore positional vs keyword arguments.
learningObjectives: Invoke the print() function with single and multiple arguments.
Understand what a function, an argument, and a function call represent in Python.
Control output formatting using the sep and end keyword parameters.

sections.heading: 1.3.1 Anatomy of the print() Function Call
sections.content:
In Python, print() is a built-in function. A function is a reusable block of code that performs a specific action.

When you call print("Hello, World!"), you provide an argument inside the parentheses. The print() function takes this argument, converts it to textual representation, writes it to standard output (the terminal), and automatically adds an invisible newline character (\n) at the end so the next print() starts on a fresh line.

codeExamples.code:
print("Programming in Python Essentials 1")
print("Notice this appears on a new line.")
codeExamples.explanation: Two sequential print calls produce two distinct lines in the output console.
codeExamples.expectedOutput:
Programming in Python Essentials 1
Notice this appears on a new line.

sections.heading: 1.3.2 Multiple Arguments and the sep & end Parameters
sections.content:
You can pass multiple arguments separated by commas:
print("My", "name", "is", "Python.")
By default, print() inserts a space character between each argument.

You can override this behavior using the keyword arguments sep and end:
• sep (separator): Defines what string is inserted between arguments (default is ' ').
• end (terminator): Defines what string is printed at the very end of the function call (default is '\n').

codeExamples.explanation: The sep parameter specifies custom hyphen separators, while end='...' prevents a newline between Loading and Done!.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What is the default value of the end keyword argument in Python's print() function?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: By default, end='\n', causing subsequent print() outputs to appear on a new line.

recap: The print() function is the universal output mechanism, highly customizable via sep and end keyword parameters.
